answer: In an agent marketplace for ember detectors, inlet valves, and timber, each seller identity must lock a $100 bond for 30 days before bidding. A contract slashes that bond if a seller signs two conflicting delivery receipts for the same order. Creating 1,000 aliases therefore ties up $100,000, and using them for provable fraud burns the posted capital. New names cannot erase the cost because every replacement needs its own bond.
